# Authentication fanout review

Check distinct accounts, time window, candidate-password cardinality, failures and successes. A small password candidate set across many accounts supports spraying; repeated failure alone does not establish that pattern. Never request or disclose actual passwords. Correlate a successful account with authorized testing and account-owner evidence before claiming compromise.

# Account session ownership

Confirmed unauthorized use of an existing account supports valid-account abuse. Do not infer credential acquisition method or an account subtype that the evidence does not establish.

On systems holding privileged logon sessions, completed unauthorized credential-process capture has critical impact. Do not claim that credentials were extracted or reused unless additional evidence establishes those actions.

# Account session ownership

A successful password or MFA check establishes authentication acceptance, not the identity of the operator. Compare device assignment, role, access scope and out-of-band account-owner confirmation. Confirmed unauthorized use of an existing account supports valid-account abuse. Do not infer credential acquisition method or an account subtype that the evidence does not establish.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.
attachments.57a8ecb0034ac2d1e9a325c6885d3be0:
# Repeated MFA prompts

Review prompt count, approval outcome, registered-device status and the account owner’s response. Many prompts can be a meaningful anomaly, but count alone does not prove coercion or bypass. An owner denial of the exact successful session materially changes the interpretation. Avoid claiming an MFA mechanism failed when only an accepted prompt is observed.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.
attachments.0a58e4158c25a1cb642942147fe897f8:
# New location review

Location changes may reflect travel, proxy use or misuse. Ask whether the device is assigned and whether the account owner confirms the session. Registration and a single approved prompt do not establish who operated the device. If travel or owner evidence is unavailable, describe the unresolved alternatives and request the narrow verification needed.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.

# New location review

Location changes may reflect travel, proxy use or misuse. Ask whether the device is assigned and whether the account owner confirms the session. Registration and a single approved prompt do not establish who operated the device. If travel or owner evidence is unavailable, describe the unresolved alternatives and request the narrow verification needed.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.
attachments.f50467ec0572355f6135baedc10d3ef9:
# Account session ownership

A successful password or MFA check establishes authentication acceptance, not the identity of the operator. Compare device assignment, role, access scope and out-of-band account-owner confirmation. Confirmed unauthorized use of an existing account supports valid-account abuse. Do not infer credential acquisition method or an account subtype that the evidence does not establish.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.
attachments.ed406113d3cc21d42d396ebc399be815:
# Authentication fanout review

Check distinct accounts, time window, candidate-password cardinality, failures and successes. A small password candidate set across many accounts supports spraying; repeated failure alone does not establish that pattern. Never request or disclose actual passwords. Correlate a successful account with authorized testing and account-owner evidence before claiming compromise.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.

RB06.title: Authentication fanout review
RB06.text:
# Authentication fanout review

Check distinct accounts, time window, candidate-password cardinality, failures and successes. A small password candidate set across many accounts supports spraying; repeated failure alone does not establish that pattern. Never request or disclose actual passwords. Correlate a successful account with authorized testing and account-owner evidence before claiming compromise.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.

RB02.title: Severity policy
RB02.text:
# Severity policy

Use severity 1 (critical) for observed restricted-data export from a critical asset or completed credential-memory capture on a critical identity system. Use 2 (high) for evidenced unauthorized remote control, account use, persistence, protection impairment or tool transfer without that critical impact. Use 3 (medium) for unresolved anomalies requiring review. Use 4 (low) for narrowly verified routine authorized activity. State the observed impact; an intimidating rule name is not evidence of impact.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.

RB08.title: Credential process memory review
RB08.text:
# Credential process memory review

Distinguish memory-read rights and a created dump from metadata queries or denied access. Check the source binary path, signature, parent and diagnostic authorization. On systems holding privileged logon sessions, completed unauthorized credential-process capture has critical impact. Do not claim that credentials were extracted or reused unless additional evidence establishes those actions.

Original guidance for this synthetic offline lab. Technique references and terms are listed in DATASET.md.
